Working in /opt/nxeon-v2 (Next.js app, branch design/v2) — a from-scratch visual/UX redesign ("Nexion") of a hosting platform's customer dashboard, built on a real backend. NXEON_SANDBOX=1 deliberately stubs exactly: Proxmox VM provisioning, Stripe card charges, DB Studio's live SQL. Everything else should be real. This is a READ-ONLY audit before production promotion — do not edit or fix anything, only report findings with file:line evidence.

Prior audits already confirmed (do not re-check, just background): order submission for VPS/Hosting/Game/Email is real and server-priced; saved payment cards (lib/stripe-cards.ts, lib/actions-saved-cards.ts) are correctly ownership-checked, impersonation-guarded, and store no raw PAN; wallet top-up (AddFundsPaymentModal.tsx) uses the Custom Checkout Stripe flow correctly.

Your job — audit the BILLING area of app/dashboard/billing and the "My Services" overview, plus supporting lib files: lib/spend-caps.ts, lib/proration.ts, lib/renewal-charge.ts, lib/renewal-quote.ts, lib/billing-terms.ts, lib/backup-upgrade.ts, components/nx/BillingView.tsx, and whatever "My Services" page/component exists (search app/dashboard for it, likely app/dashboard/services or similar, and lib/nx/services.ts which was referenced by ServicePreview audit).

Check and report on:
1. **Auto-renewal charging**: is there a real worker/cron job that actually charges customers for renewals (search worker/*.ts for "renew" and lib/renewal-charge.ts)? Does it correctly use the wallet-first-then-card fallback pattern seen elsewhere? Any risk of double-charging (no idempotency key/guard) or silently failing to renew (service gets cut off with no charge attempt logged)?
2. **Outstanding balance / dunning**: if a renewal charge fails, is there a real "outstanding balance" state shown to the customer with a real "settle now" action, or is this only partially wired?
3. **Spend caps** (lib/spend-caps.ts): is this a real enforced limit somewhere in the order/renewal path, or a schema/settings field nothing reads?
4. **Proration** (lib/proration.ts): used correctly for plan upgrades/downgrades/cancellations — verify the math path is real Prisma-backed, not a UI-only estimate that diverges from what's actually charged.
5. **Invoices/receipts**: is there a real invoice history the customer can view/download, backed by real Stripe invoice objects or real DB records, or is billing history UI-only/incomplete?
6. **"My Services" page**: does it correctly aggregate ALL of a customer's real services (servers, hosting accounts, domains, email) from Prisma, including their ServicePreview images, or does anything on this page use placeholder/hardcoded content?
7. Any NEW-this-redesign billing feature you notice that isn't in this list — flag it and audit it the same way (real vs stub).

Report as a table: Feature | REAL / PARTIAL / STUB | evidence (file:line) | what's missing. Keep under 700 words. Do not modify any files.

55	  gamePlan: { name: string; priceCents: number; termMonths: number } | null;
56	  dedicatedIp: unknown | null;
57	  /** Paid backup retention tier. A full Server row supplies it; synthetic callers must pass it. */

117	  // plan was configured with (a pre-existing game server was created with
118	  // `termMonths = gamePlan.termMonths`, which the admin can set 1..36). We therefore
119	  // read the game term back RAW (clamped >= 1) rather than through `vpsTerm`, whose
120	  // fallback would collapse a non-standard legacy value (say 3) to monthly and
121	  // change that server's renewal cadence. For the seeded games (all `termMonths: 1`)
122	  // and any new Monthly/Annual order this is identical to the standard path.

125	  // falling back to the live setting for legacy/monthly rows. Both halves resolve
126	  // the same number, so an annual sub renews at the sold rate.

128	  // Extra root disk is billed EVERY cycle at the current per-GB price. Game plans
129	  // are a flat all-in price and never carry the add-on lines.
130	  const extraDiskMonthlyCents = isGame ? 0 : extraDiskCentsAt(server.extraDiskGB, prices.extraDiskPerGbCents);

145	    : 0;
146	  // LEGACY GUARD. Game servers sold BEFORE terms existed carry no frozen annual rate
147	  // (`annualDiscountPct == null`) and always renewed at the plan's FLAT `priceCents`,
148	  // with no term discount ever applied. Preserve that exactly so no pre-existing game
149	  // server's renewal moves — only servers sold through the new term-aware flow (which
150	  // always stamps a frozen `annualDiscountPct`) are priced with `termPriceCents`.
151	  //
152	  // GUARD ON isGame FIRST. This value is only USED in the isGame branch below, but a
153	  // bare ternary evaluates it for EVERY server — and a VPS `PricedServer` (e.g. the one
154	  // the deploy wizard builds, `gamePlan: null`, no `annualDiscountPct`) then hits the
155	  // `annualDiscountPct == null` arm and dereferences `server.gamePlan!.priceCents` on a
156	  // null, crashing the whole deploy page with "Cannot read properties of null". Compute
157	  // 0 for non-game so the null is never touched.
158	  const gameTotalCents = !isGame
159	    ? 0
160	    : server.annualDiscountPct == null
161	      ? server.gamePlan!.priceCents
162	      : termPriceCents(gameMonthlyCents, months, annualPct);
163	  const netCents = isGame
164	    ? gameTotalCents +
165	      (server.dedicatedIp ? prices.ipMonthlyCents * months : 0)
166	    : vpsTermPriceCents(server.plan.priceCents, months, annualPct) +
167	      // Bill the IP surcharge only when the server ACTUALLY holds a dedicated IP,
168	      // not off the intent flag — a NAT-fallback server must never be charged for
169	      // an IP it never received.
170	      (server.dedicatedIp ? prices.ipMonthlyCents * months : 0) +
171	      extraDiskCents +
172	      backupCents;
173	  // VAT/GST on the pre-tax subtotal. Default rate 0 keeps `totalCents === netCents`
174	  // for every caller that does not pass the owner's rate (Finding 1).
175	  const taxRatePercent =
176	    Number.isFinite(prices.taxRatePercent) && (prices.taxRatePercent ?? 0) > 0 ? prices.taxRatePercent! : 0;

179	    months,
180	    netCents,
181	    taxCents,
182	    taxRatePercent,
183	    totalCents: netCents + taxCents,
184	    extraDiskCents,
185	    extraDiskMonthlyCents,
186	    backupCents,
187	    backupMonthlyCents,
188	    label: isGame ? server.gamePlan!.name : `${server.plan.name} VPS`,
189	  };

# Nxeon v2 — the "Nexion" design fork **This is not the production tree.** It is a full fork of the Nxeon platform with a from-scratch visual language called **Nexion** built over the real backend. The code is real, the database is real, the money paths are real code — but `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, so no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged. Read `docs/NEXION-V2.md` next. This file is the operating manual; that one is the direction and the history of what has been built. --- ## Where you are, and what that changes This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's commits. The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously. ## The tree | | | |---|---| | Path | `/opt/nxeon-v2` | | Branch | `design/v2` | | Service | `nxeon-v2-web` on port **3021** | | Public URL | https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud | | Database | `nxeon_v2` on localhost — **separate** from prod and from the primary's own copy | | Logins | `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt` (admin + a design customer account) | | Build log | `/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log` | `rebuild.sh` skips the marketing site by default (~137 of ~195 route files, and it dominates a build we run by hand after every change). `NX_FULL=1 ./rebuild.sh` builds everything — do that before any staging or prod pass. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. Use `scripts/node1.sh` rather than raw ssh — quoting a psql call through two levels of ssh is where this reliably goes wrong: ```bash scripts/node1.sh cards "dashboard" # find concept cards by title scripts/node1.sh board # list that card's attachments scripts/node1.sh pull # copy them to /tmp/board/ scripts/node1.sh db "select …" # read-only query against PROD scripts/node1.sh sh '' # anything else ``` **That grant is wide, and node-1 runs every customer VM, the production database and the mail server. Treat it as read-only.** Never write to the prod DB (the `db` subcommand refuses obvious writes, which is a guard against a slip, not a security boundary), never edit `/opt/nxeon`, never build there, never restart a prod service. If you genuinely need to change something on node-1, **stop and ask the owner first.** ## Rules that are not negotiable 1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not reintroduce that shape. When a source cannot answer, say so; never render a `0` that reads as a real measurement. 2. **Never run builds in `/opt/nxeon`.** That is live production; clobbering its `.next` has taken the admin panel down before. 3. **Never `pkill -f` by pattern on either box.** `pkill -f "next start"` restarted live production once. Kill by port PID or systemd unit. 4. **Never `git add -A` in a symlinked worktree** — it can replace prod's real `node_modules` with a self-referential symlink. 5. **Ask before touching credentials** on live customer infrastructure, and before spending on any paid third-party tool. 6. **Never send a support-ticket reply** without explicit sign-off. 7. **`/opt/nxeon-sandbox` belongs to a different session.** Leave it alone. 8. Secrets are gitignored. Never commit `.env` or a credentials file. ## Verification discipline A change is not done until it is **deployed and screenshotted**. There is a login-and-capture script: ```bash node scripts/shot.mjs /tmp/out /dashboard/directory /dashboard/settings # defaults to the design customer account; override with NX_EMAIL / NX_PASS ``` Playwright scripts must live inside `/opt/nxeon-v2` so the module resolves. Read the PNG back and actually look at it — a sliced game wordmark, a clipped top bar and an empty Mods tab were all invisible in the code and obvious in a screenshot. ## Things that have already cost hours here - **Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls.** Always `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && …`. - **`git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks.** Write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`. - **`git bundle create f A..B` with two raw SHAs** makes a bundle with no refs, which git refuses as empty. The tip must be a named ref: `A..design/v2`. - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` aurora layer paints above static content.** Page content needs `relative z-[1]`. - **A `backdrop-filter` ancestor becomes the containing block for `fixed` children** — `createPortal` to `document.body` instead. - **Never size a fixed overlay from a header's height.** That is the header's bottom edge only when nothing sits above it, and the sandbox banner does. Let the layout place things. - **`mask-composite` is unevenly supported** — nest two single-axis masks. - **An `` that fails before hydration never fires `onError`.** Check `el.complete && el.naturalWidth === 0` on mount. - **`fetch` cannot report request-body progress in any browser.** Upload progress needs `XMLHttpRequest.upload.onprogress`. - **Shell-level React providers are easy to drop.** The Nexion shell omitted `ComposeProvider`, then `TerminalDockProvider`, then `MatrixProvider` — each took a whole feature down invisibly, because the crash only appears on a route a smoke test does not walk. Anything added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` must be added to `components/nx/Shell.tsx` too. ## Conventions inherited from the platform (still true here) - Every VM state change goes through a `Job` row. The web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly. - One in-flight job per server. - Wallet amounts are integer cents. - Admin-only actions call `requireAdmin()` and refuse to render while impersonating. - Charts are dependency-free SVG in `components/ui/charts.tsx`. Do not add a charting library. ## Inherited instructions that do NOT apply here The production `CLAUDE.md` this replaced is kept at `docs/CLAUDE-production-inherited.md` for reference. It describes the PRIMARY node. To avoid a very expensive mistake: - **Do not** run `systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — that is production. This tree's unit is `nxeon-v2-web`. - **Do not** publish docs to `revsports.ca/docs` from here. - **Do not** run `scripts/promote-production.sh` or `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`. - There is no post-commit auto-push hook on node-2, and there should not be: `design/v2` is a design fork, not something to push to `origin` casually.

22	 * There is deliberately NO cap parameter, and re-adding one would reopen a money
23	 * bug. `expiresAt` only ever moves forward in exchange for payment: the initial
24	 * order term (lib/order.ts, lib/actions.ts placeOrder), `renewNow`
25	 * (lib/actions.ts) and the auto-renew sweep (worker/billing.ts) each advance it by
26	 * exactly `termMonths` and charge `vpsTermPriceCents` for those months. So every
27	 * month between `now` and `expiresAt` is a month the customer has actually bought,
28	 * however many terms of "Renew now" are stacked up in there, and the honest
29	 * prorated figure covers all of them.
30	 *
31	 * This used to take `capMonths`, and that optional knob is precisely how the two
32	 * directions drifted apart: the upgrade path (lib/resize.ts) passed no cap while
33	 * the downgrade path (lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts) passed `server.termMonths`.
34	 * A customer who had stacked "Renew now" out to 36 months on a 12-month term was
35	 * charged $544.32 to move Starter -> Max and credited only $181.44 to move
36	 * straight back — the platform kept $362.88 it never earned. Four call sites
37	 * (two servers, two pickers) had to agree on that argument by convention, and they
38	 * did not. With the knob gone every caller gets the same number from the same
39	 * one-argument call, so the round-trip invariant is structural instead of a
40	 * comment someone has to honour.
41	 *
42	 * A cap was never what protected the credit side either. The credit is
43	 * `(effective(from) - effective(to)) x months` priced through `prorateDeltaCents`
44	 * at the term-discounted AND promo-reduced rate, while the renewal paths charge
45	 * the term price with no promo applied — so the credit for a given month is
46	 * strictly less than what that month cost. What made the old credit a money
47	 * printer was the RAW LIST-price delta it used before 2026-07-25, not the number
48	 * of months it spanned.
49	 */
50	export function remainingMonths(expiresAt: Date | null, now: number): number {
51	  if (!expiresAt) return 0;
52	  return Math.max(0, (expiresAt.getTime() - now) / MS_PER_AVG_MONTH);
53	}
54	
55	/**
56	 * The rate basis for a proration, resolved from what the server row records.
57	 *
58	 * `Server.termPromoPercent` is the percent off the term-discounted monthly rate
59	 * that the months currently left on `expiresAt` were ACTUALLY sold at. NULL means
60	 * the row predates that column and the rate is unknown.
61	 *
62	 * ─── WHY NULL MUST NOT FALL THROUGH TO `currentPromo(now)` ──────────────────
63	 * That was the bug, fixed 2026-07-26. `prorateDeltaCents` used to default its rate
64	 * basis to the seasonal promo running at the instant of the call. Promos rotate by
65	 * calendar date from a 15% Launch Sale up to 45% for Cyber Monday (lib/promotions.ts),
66	 * so both halves of a round trip were priced off a number the CUSTOMER got to choose
67	 * by picking the date. Upgrade on Cyber Monday: the delta is charged at 55% of the
68	 * honest rate. Downgrade back in mid-January: the same delta is credited at 85%.
69	 * The 30-point spread x plan delta x every remaining month falls straight into the
70	 * wallet, repeatable every promo cycle, with the platform's own marketing calendar
71	 * published as the timetable. On the pinned catalogue (Starter 899 -> Max 3299, a
72	 * 36-month term) that is $207.36 of minted cash per cycle for zero net change.
73	 *
74	 * It was also simply the wrong rate. lib/promotions.ts states in its opening line
75	 * that a promo discounts a customer's FIRST TERM only and that renewals never get
76	 * it — yet this priced a mid-term plan change, on months that may well have been
77	 * bought at a renewal's full price, off a promo the customer was never sold.
78	 *
79	 * ─── THE FALLBACK, AND WHY IT IS THE DEEPEST DISCOUNT AND NOT FULL PRICE ────
80	 * The obvious conservative guess is "assume they paid full list" (percent 0). It is
81	 * the wrong direction and it MINTS MONEY. A credit is monotonically INCREASING in
82	 * the rate basis, so percent 0 produces the LARGEST credit this function can emit.
83	 * A customer who really bought Max on a 36-month term during Cyber Monday paid
84	 * 0.55 x 2639 = 1451c per month-equivalent; a downgrade to Starter priced at
85	 * percent 0 credits (2639 - 719) = 1920c per month — 469c/month MORE than they ever
86	 * paid, so 36 months hands back $168.84 of cash they never spent AND leaves them a
87	 * running Starter VPS for three years.
88	 *
89	 * So the fallback goes the other way: assume the LEAST the platform has ever
90	 * charged (`deepestPromoPercent()`). Under that basis the credit is bounded below
91	 * the real cash for every rate the customer could actually have been sold. The
92	 * price of being wrong in this direction is a cheaper upgrade for an unknown-rate
93	 * server — a pricing concession, not a printer: it can only ever reduce revenue
94	 * collected, never push cash OUT, and because BOTH directions read this same
95	 * resolved number a round trip still nets to exactly zero. Given the choice
96	 * between under-charging and over-refunding, this file's entire incident history
97	 * says take the under-charge.
98	 *
99	 * ── WHAT THAT ARGUMENT NOW COSTS (noted 2026-09-11) ─────────────────────────
100	 * It was written when the deepest promo was the 45% Cyber Monday. The catalogue
101	 * since became a SINGLE always-on promo — FIRST_MONTH_FREE at 100% — so
102	 * `deepestPromoPercent()` returns 100, `discountedCents` flattens BOTH sides of
103	 * the delta to zero, and the "concession" is the entire price: an unknown-rate
104	 * server upgrades for free. The reasoning above still holds in shape (it cannot
105	 * push cash out, and a round trip still nets to zero); it is the magnitude that
106	 * stopped being a concession.
107	 *
108	 * Deliberately NOT changed here, because both directions have a documented
109	 * failure mode in this file and picking one reprices real customers. It is
110	 * unreachable on live data — every Server row carries a backfilled rate, and the
111	 * single null row is free with no expiry, so proration is skipped — but it is one
112	 * unstamped row away from mattering. lib/game-resize.ts refuses outright rather
113	 * than quoting a zero it cannot justify; the other callers do not.
114	 *
115	 * (After scripts/backfill-term-promo-percent.ts this branch is unreachable on live
116	 * data — every row carries a rate derived from what it was actually invoiced.
117	 * Verified again 2026-09-11: one null row, free and unexpiring, so never priced.)
118	 */
119	export function resolveTermPromoPercent(termPromoPercent: number | null | undefined): number {
120	  if (termPromoPercent === null || termPromoPercent === undefined) return deepestPromoPercent();
121	  // A stored value outside 0-100 would invert or amplify the delta; clamp rather
122	  // than trust, since this number is a direct multiplier on money.
123	  return Math.min(100, Math.max(0, termPromoPercent));
124	}
125	
126	/**
127	 * The value-weighted blend of the rate the remaining months are already on and the
128	 * rate a freshly-added block of months is being sold at.
129	 *
130	 * `termPromoPercent` is ONE scalar covering every month left on `expiresAt`, but
131	 * months get added to that window at different rates: an intro-discounted first
132	 * term, then renewals at full price, and occasionally an admin gift at no price at
133	 * all. Overwriting the scalar on each addition would silently reprice the months
134	 * already in there — and in the profitable direction. Concretely: buy a 36-month
135	 * term at 45% off, click "Renew now" once (which honestly charges full price for 36
136	 * more months), and a plain overwrite would re-rate the original 36 discounted
137	 * months to full price too, restoring the exact same spread this field exists to
138	 * kill. Blending keeps the total cash value of the remaining window invariant:
139	 * added months contribute their own rate and nothing reprices what came before.
140	 *
141	 * The result is deliberately NOT rounded to a whole percent, which is why the
142	 * column is a Float: 36 months at 45% off plus 36 renewed months at full price is
143	 * exactly 22.5% off, and rounding that to 23 shaves $7.20 off the $1,071.36 credit
144	 * those 72 months are worth. Rounding here would also compound over a server's
145	 * lifetime, once per renewal. (It could never break the round-trip invariant —
146	 * both directions read the same stored scalar whatever it holds — but "symmetric"
147	 * and "correct" are different properties and this file owes the customer both.)
148	 */
149	export function prorateBlendPercent(opts: {
150	  /** Rate the months already on the clock were sold at (already resolved). */
151	  currentPercent: number;
152	  /** How many months are already on the clock. */
153	  currentMonths: number;
154	  /** Rate the newly-added months are being sold at. 0 = full price, 100 = gifted. */
155	  addedPercent: number;
156	  /** How many months are being added. Non-positive => nothing to blend. */
157	  addedMonths: number;
158	}): number {
159	  const cur = Math.min(100, Math.max(0, opts.currentPercent));
160	  const add = Math.min(100, Math.max(0, opts.addedPercent));
161	  const curMonths = Math.max(0, opts.currentMonths);
162	  const addMonths = Math.max(0, opts.addedMonths);
163	  const total = curMonths + addMonths;
164	  // Nothing on the clock and nothing added: keep the incoming rate rather than
165	  // divide by zero. (Also the honest answer for "term shortened, none added" —
166	  // fewer months at the same rate, which is exactly what the caller wants.)
167	  if (total <= 0) return cur;
168	  const value = curMonths * (1 - cur / 100) + addMonths * (1 - add / 100);
169	  const pct = 100 * (1 - value / total);
170	  // Snap off binary-float noise only: 36mo at 45% blended with 36mo at 0% is
171	  // exactly 22.5 but computes as 22.500000000000007, and blending a rate with
172	  // itself must be an exact no-op rather than drifting a hair on every renewal.
173	  // Six decimal places is a millionth of a percentage point — far below a cent on
174	  // any conceivable term — while leaving every genuine fraction intact.
175	  return Math.min(100, Math.max(0, Math.round(pct * 1e6) / 1e6));
176	}
177	
178	/**
179	 * The prorated difference between two monthly plan prices over the remaining
180	 * term, priced against THE RATE THIS SERVER'S TERM WAS ACTUALLY SOLD AT.
181	 *
182	 * Why the rate is a required argument (2026-07-26): it used to default to
183	 * `currentPromo(now)`, which handed the customer the pricing basis for both halves
184	 * of a round trip — see `resolveTermPromoPercent` for the full arbitrage. Making it
185	 * required means a call site cannot forget it; there is no basis to fall back TO.
186	 *
187	 * Why this exists at all (2026-07-25): proration used the raw list monthly delta
188	 * while the original purchase applied BOTH the term discount (lib/order.ts) and the
189	 * seasonal promo. Upgrading therefore cost far more than buying the target plan
190	 * outright for the same end date — on a 36-month term with a 30% promo running,
191	 * $1,044.45 to upgrade versus $665.08 fresh: the customer overpaid $379.37. The
192	 * mirror image was worse in kind: the downgrade CREDIT used the same undiscounted
193	 * delta, so it refunded more than was ever paid.
194	 *
195	 * Both directions price off the SAME function and the SAME persisted scalar, so
196	 * they cannot drift apart:
197	 *   effective monthly (term discount) → term's sold rate → × months left.
198	 */
199	export function prorateDeltaCents(opts: {
200	  fromMonthlyCents: number;
201	  toMonthlyCents: number;
202	  termMonths: number;
203	  monthsRemaining: number;
204	  /**
205	   * `Server.termPromoPercent` — percent off that THIS server's remaining months
206	   * were sold at. Pass the row value straight through, null and all; it is
207	   * resolved here so every call site resolves it identically.
208	   */
209	  termPromoPercent: number | null;
210	  /**
211	   * The admin-configured ANNUAL discount (percent) from `annualDiscountPct()`.
212	   *
213	   * OPTIONAL — unlike the renewal-pricing field in lib/renewal-charge.ts, which is
214	   * required. Two reasons it is safe optional here: it only bites a 12-month server
215	   * (every other `termMonths` ignores it via `termDiscountPct`), and when omitted it
216	   * falls back to the shipped default — the same number the annual term shipped at.
217	   * Server-side resize paths (lib/resize.ts, lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts) and
218	   * the resize UIs DO pass the live value, so an annual server's mid-term upgrade
219	   * and downgrade credit price against the SAME rate its order and renewals use;
220	   * left off, the maths is unchanged for every non-annual term and matches the
221	   * default for annual.
222	   */
223	  annualDiscountPct?: number;
224	}): number {
225	  const pct = resolveTermPromoPercent(opts.termPromoPercent);
226	  const eff = (monthly: number) =>
227	    discountedCents(vpsEffectiveMonthly(monthly, opts.termMonths, opts.annualDiscountPct), pct);
228	  const delta = eff(opts.toMonthlyCents) - eff(opts.fromMonthlyCents);
229	  return Math.round(delta * Math.max(0, opts.monthsRemaining));
230	}
231	
232	/** Upgrade charge — never negative. */
233	export function prorateUpgradeCents(opts: Parameters<typeof prorateDeltaCents>[0]): number {
234	  return Math.max(0, prorateDeltaCents(opts));
235	}
236	
237	/** Downgrade credit — never negative; caller passes from=old, to=new. */
238	export function prorateDowngradeCreditCents(
239	  opts: Parameters<typeof prorateDeltaCents>[0]
240	): number {
241	  return Math.max(0, -prorateDeltaCents(opts));
242	}
243	
244	/**
245	 * The prorated refund owed for the UNUSED portion of a paid term on IMMEDIATE
246	 * cancellation (Finding 2), in cents — the value of every remaining month priced at
247	 * the SAME effective rate the term was sold at, computed as a downgrade all the way
248	 * to a $0 plan (so it reuses `prorateDowngradeCreditCents`).
249	 *
250	 * NEVER OVER-REFUNDS: the per-month credit is the term-discounted, promo-reduced rate,
251	 * while every month on the clock was collected at AT LEAST that (renewals charge the
252	 * full term price with no promo), and `expiresAt` only advances in exchange for
253	 * payment — so the credit is strictly ≤ what was actually paid for the unused time.
254	 * Game servers return 0 (they are sold at a flat game-plan price, not the base VPS
255	 * `planMonthlyCents` this values against, so any non-zero figure could over-refund).
256	 *
257	 * `annualDiscountPct` must be pre-resolved by the caller to
258	 * `frozenAnnualDiscountPct(server) ?? liveRate`, mirroring the resize/downgrade paths.
259	 */
260	export function terminationRefundCents(opts: {
261	  isFree: boolean;
262	  expiresAt: Date | null;
263	  isGame: boolean;
264	  planMonthlyCents: number;
265	  termMonths: number;
266	  termPromoPercent: number | null;
267	  annualDiscountPct: number;
268	  /**
269	   * The plan-portion cash actually collected for this term (net of promo AND coupon,
270	   * add-ons excluded), from `Server.refundableTermCents`. When present it is the
271	   * AUTHORITATIVE basis — the refund is this figure prorated over the unused months,
272	   * which is exact, coupon-aware and provably ≤ paid. Only when it is null (legacy
273	   * rows predating the column) do we fall back to the `termPromoPercent` formula,
274	   * which never over-refunds but reads $0 for the 100-stamped common case.
275	   */
276	  refundableTermCents?: number | null;
277	  now?: number;
278	}): number {
279	  if (opts.isFree || !opts.expiresAt || opts.isGame) return 0;
280	  const rem = remainingMonths(opts.expiresAt, opts.now ?? Date.now());
281	  // AUTHORITATIVE PATH: prorate the real cash collected. `rem` is clamped ≥ 0 and can
282	  // reach at most `termMonths` (expiresAt only advances one term per payment), so the
283	  // ratio is ≤ 1 and the refund is ≤ the cash collected — never an over-refund. The
284	  // final clamp is belt-and-braces against a stale/renewed expiresAt drift.
285	  if (opts.refundableTermCents != null && opts.termMonths > 0) {
286	    const basis = Math.max(0, opts.refundableTermCents);
287	    const refund = Math.round((basis * Math.min(rem, opts.termMonths)) / opts.termMonths);
288	    return Math.max(0, Math.min(refund, basis));
289	  }
290	  // LEGACY FALLBACK: value each unused month at the term-discounted, promo-reduced rate.
291	  return prorateDowngradeCreditCents({
292	    fromMonthlyCents: opts.planMonthlyCents,
293	    toMonthlyCents: 0,
294	    termMonths: opts.termMonths,
295	    termPromoPercent: opts.termPromoPercent,
296	    annualDiscountPct: opts.annualDiscountPct,
297	    monthsRemaining: rem,
298	  });
299	}
